newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down, follow regional markets.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down, follow regional markets.

text.p: Thai stocks fell 1.46 percent in thin trade on Monday in line with declines on Wall Street and on regional markets earlier in the day, brokers said.

The SET index moved in negative zone all day and ended 16.09 points down at 1,086.23 on 1.9 billion baht trade. Decliners led gainers 257 to 66 while 99 issues were unchanged. The SET-50 index dipped 1.31 points to 82.71.

"Market sentiment was poor due to a sharp fall on Wall Street on Friday and other regional markets on Monday. Investors also awaited the August consumer price index that was to be released by the commerce ministry," a broker said.
"Investors were reluctant to invest as they awaited the August price index to be released by the commerce ministry," Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities said.
After the market closed, the Commerce Ministry said the year-on-year consumer price index for August rose 5.5 percent versus a 5.4 percent increase in July.
Virat said the fall on Monday was of not surprising because the SET was already battered by negative central bank economic indicators released last week.
The indicators showed still-slack exports growth.
Large capitalised stocks fell on Monday. Bangkok Bank declined two baht to 216 while Finance One slipped one to 105 and Shinawatra Computer and Communications dipped eight to 384.
Support is seen by some brokers at 1,072-point and resistance at 1,095 on Tuesday.
